name: Rain
current_role: Likely Rainer (Reiner) Schmidt-Ruthenbeck, co-owner with brother Michael of the family's Metro AG stake
profile: Entry appears to be a truncated 'Rainer Schmidt-Ruthenbeck' (Germany, listed jointly with brother Michael). Born 1941, son of Metro co-founder Wilhelm Schmidt-Ruthenbeck; the brothers' family holding owned roughly 13-16% of German retailer Metro AG. Lives in Duisburg; keeps a very low profile.
interesting_fact: Forbes ranked Michael and Reiner Schmidt-Ruthenbeck jointly at #722 on its 2016 billionaires list with US$2.4 billion.
deep_cut_fact: His family (the Karl Schmidt family of Duisburg merchants) set up Stiftung Mercator in 1996, one of Germany's largest private foundations, named after the cartographer Gerhard Mercator, who lived in Duisburg for decades.
notes: Identity inferred: input name 'Rain' with shared_with 'Schmidt-Ruthenbeck Bros., Michael' (Forbes 1997) most likely = Rainer Schmidt-Ruthenbeck. Extremely private; no personal channels. The only route is via the family foundation (Stiftung Mercator), and it is indirect.

name: Raja Bagmane
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Bagmane Group (Bagmane Developers Pvt Ltd), Bengaluru
profile: Bengaluru real-estate developer who founded Bagmane Group in 1996 and built it into one of the city's largest commercial/tech-park landlords (Bagmane Tech Park, Bagmane World Technology Center; ~30 mn sq ft operational). Blackstone took a minority stake in 2024, and the group sponsors Bagmane Prime Office REIT, which has listed in India. His sons Aditya and Shashank are directors.
interesting_fact: Bagmane Tech Park in C V Raman Nagar, launched in 2001, was one of Bengaluru's earliest IT parks; the group's portfolio is now hosted in a Blackstone-backed listed REIT.
notes: Low media profile; rarely gives interviews. The published email is a general company enquiries inbox. A data-center/tech-park angle is relevant: Bagmane hosts big tech occupiers in Bengaluru. His sons may be easier to reach for a conversation.

name: Jose Batista Sobrinho
current_role: Founder of JBS S.A. (honorary patriarch; no operational role since the 1980s apart from a stint as interim CEO in 2017)
profile: 'Zé Mineiro' (b. 1933, Carmo do Rio Claro, Minas Gerais) opened a small butcher shop, Casa de Carnes Mineira, in Anápolis, Goiás, in 1953. It grew into JBS, named after his initials and now the world's largest meat processor, run by his sons Joesley and Wesley. In June 2025 he rang the NYSE opening bell for JBS's US listing.
interesting_fact: At around 91, he rang the opening bell at the New York Stock Exchange on 25 June 2025 when JBS began trading in New York, with his sons alongside him.
deep_cut_fact: His business first took off by selling beef to the construction companies building the new capital, Brasília, in the late 1950s. That was the springboard for what became JBS.
notes: He is in his 90s and has no public channels of his own. Any approach would go through JBS/J&F press. Hurun last listed him separately in 2014; the family wealth is mostly attributed to his sons.

name: Peter Hargreaves
current_role: Co-founder of Hargreaves Lansdown; backer/partner of Blue Whale Capital (left HL board Oct 2025; son Robert took his seat)
profile: Clitheroe-born chartered accountant who co-founded Hargreaves Lansdown with Stephen Lansdown from a Bristol spare bedroom in 1981, building the UK's largest retail investment platform. HL was taken private in a £5.4bn takeover in 2025, and he remains a major shareholder. He seeded fund manager Blue Whale Capital in 2017 and is the main stakeholder in satellite ground-station firm GomSpace.
interesting_fact: He came ninth among the UK's biggest taxpayers in 2021, with a reported tax bill of £91.4 million that year.
deep_cut_fact: An early backer of hydrogen: he joined the board of electrolyser maker ITM Power as a non-executive director in 2004, invested heavily, and recruited Dr Graham Cooley as its CEO in 2009. Before HL, he worked as a computer salesman.

public_contacts.value: Edelman Smithfield (Blue Whale Capital press): bluewhale@edelmansmithfield.com

notes: Outspoken and interview-friendly in the UK financial press. His energy and space investments (ITM Power hydrogen, GomSpace satellites) fit the podcast's angle. Blue Whale is the best route to him. Brexit donations are politically sensitive, so avoid leading with them.

name: Geoffrey Kwok
current_role: Director, Empire Group Holdings (Hong Kong); Non-Executive Director, Sun Hung Kai Properties
profile: Eldest son of the late Walter Kwok (ex-chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties) and grandson of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng. He studied economics at Yale, earned a Stanford MBA and worked as a Morgan Stanley investment banker. After his father died in 2018, he and his brother Jonathan took over Empire Group Holdings, which has invested over HK$29bn in property since 2010. He also joined the SHKP board.
interesting_fact: Empire Group's 'E' logomark is derived from Walter Kwok's own signature; the rest of the word 'Empire' is meant to be completed by the succeeding generation.
deep_cut_fact: The family's Walter & Wendy Kwok Family Foundation has donated to Hong Kong's Foodlink Foundation (hot meals, food waste from hotels) since 2011. Empire also runs a Kwok Scholars programme for tertiary students and opened Kimpton Tsim Sha Tsui in March 2026.
notes: Low profile. Empire Group is the more direct route, because SHKP press is controlled by the other branch of the family. Avoid the family-feud history.

name: Satyanarayana Chava
profile: Organic chemist (PhD) who spent about a decade in pharma, at Ranbaxy and then at Matrix Labs, where he rose to COO. He founded Laurus Labs in Hyderabad in 2005 as an R&D firm. It now supplies APIs and formulations for HIV, cancer, asthma and diabetes drugs and has expanded into CDMO and biotech. He still spends about 25% of his time in the labs.
interesting_fact: He is a named co-inventor on about 145 patents granted to Laurus Labs, and in his spare time he enjoys cooking Indian food and sweets.
deep_cut_fact: As founder and first employee he never held 50% of Laurus Labs. In 2006, a year after founding, he set aside 5% of the company's equity for employee stock options.
notes: He won EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2021 (Life Sciences & Healthcare category), and he serves on the USP board of trustees. I found no dedicated press email; the secretarial inbox is the published investor channel.
